the tissue culture infectivity of infectious bursal virus is determined by different amino acids in VP-2.
the amino acid residues at positions 144 and 145 are crucial for tissue culture infectiosity.
the tissue culture infectivity of two strains of infectious bursa disease virus is determined at different sites in VP2.

the molecular mechanisms that are responsible for tissue culture infectivities of different IBDV strains.
the development of a reverse genetics system for infectious bursal disease viruses.

the tissue culture infectivity of IBDV is determined by distinct residues in VP2 of different strains of IBDV.

the ability to replicate and produce infectious progeny virus in tissue culture is determined by distinct VP2 amino acids, which are strain-specific.

the amino acid sequence of VP2 is responsible for the different tissue culture phenotypes of IBDV-BC and IBDV-VC.
